conventions.convention: Admissible sequences have positive entries and satisfy i_j ≥ 2i_{j+1}; the empty sequence is the unit with degree and excess zero. Excess is i_1−i_2−⋯−i_k.
Thom stabilization adjoins the specified positive coordinate line first, using ε¹⊕γ_r and S¹∧T_r. Stable homotopy is a sequential colimit over a legal cofinal tail.

Stable Thom cohomology here is the degreewise compatible-tuple inverse limit, with backwards maps σ⁻¹α_r*. It is a Thom module, not a reduced cup ring or an asserted represented-spectrum cohomology identification.
One homogeneous basis of Q=M/A⁺M and one degree-preserving section are fixed globally and shared by every detector rank; B(r) contains exactly generators of degree d<r.
The finite detector's mod-two cohomology comparison is strict: k<2r, with no assertion at k=2r.
Integral comparison gives isomorphisms below 2r−1 and a surjection at 2r−1; homotopy isomorphisms extend through 2r−2. Stable degree n uses r≥n+2.
Rational Hurewicz uses the actual rationalized Hurewicz map for (c−1)-connected CW complexes, c≥2, in c≤i≤2c−2, without finite-type assumptions.
Gauss normalization uses polar decomposition in a supplied tangent metric. Monomorphisms and orthonormal Stiefel frames are separate spaces, related by deformation retraction.
The positively parametrized round circle has rotation number +1; domain reversal negates it. The invariant belongs to the parametrized oriented immersion.
Stiefel fibres are connected in codimension at least one and simply connected in codimension at least two. Difference-class identifications depend on a reference section and disk transport.
The oriented collapse convention places the normal orientation before the tangent orientation. Product orientations order the manifold factors.

General Pontryagin-class multiplicativity and tangent/normal inversion are used away from two; integral characteristic-number identities follow because torsion evaluates to zero. No general integral class identity is asserted.
On complex projective space x=c₁(γ*) has positive top pairing in the complex orientation.

The triangular matrix uses Newton power-sum products and labeled refinement of partitions; the ordinary Pontryagin-number matrix need only be invertible. The empty partition gives the positive point and matrix (1).

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. The universal real and oriented Thom spaces, with the specified coordinate-first stabilization maps, form the two sequential Thom prespectra MO and MSO. Their stable homotopy groups are the colimits of π_{n+r} of their levels over legal tails.
Assume AC. For each n≥0, the stable group π_n(MO)=colim_r π_{r+n}(T_r) maps injectively to V_n=F₂^{B_n} by the compatible detector coordinates D_{r,n}, using the cofinal tail r≥n+2.

Assume AC. For every n≥0, collapse induces abelian-group isomorphisms Ω_n^O≅π_n(MO) and Ω_n^SO≅π_n(MSO), with inverse given by transverse zero preimages; these respect disjoint union, products and null-cobordism.

Assume AC. If a based CW complex X is (c−1)-connected with c≥2, the natural actual rationalized Hurewicz map π_i(X)⊗_Z Q→H_i(X;Q) is an isomorphism for c≤i≤2c−2. Lower positive rational homology vanishes. No finite-type, countability or finite-CW hypothesis is imposed, and no injectivity at 2c−1 is claimed.

Assume AC. For the connected graded bialgebra A and connected graded A-module coalgebra M with the stated unital action and coproduct compatibility, injectivity of a↦au implies that every graded section of M→Q=M/A⁺M induces an A-module isomorphism A⊗Q→M. No commutativity, antipode or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.
Assume AC. For q≥1, H*(K_q;F₂) is the polynomial algebra on the actual classes Sq^Iι_q for admissible I with e(I)<q, including the empty sequence, in degree q+|I|.
Assume AC. For the detector f_r:T_r→P_r, the pullback f_r*:H̃ᵏ(P_r;F₂)→H̃ᵏ(T_r;F₂) is an isomorphism for every k<2r. No comparison is asserted at k=2r.
Assume AC. For f_r:T_r→P_r, f_{r*}:H_i(T_r;Z)→H_i(P_r;Z) is an isomorphism for i<2r−1 and a surjection for i=2r−1. No endpoint injectivity is asserted.
Assume AC. For r≥2, f_r induces π_i(T_r)≅π_i(P_r) for 1≤i≤2r−2. On π_{r+n}, for 0≤n≤r−2, the target is F₂^{B_n} and its coordinates are evaluation on the chosen stable Thom classes.

Assume AC. At sufficiently large rank, tangent Stiefel–Whitney and Pontryagin numbers equal evaluations on the collapse class of universal Thom-module classes obtained by substituting inverse normal characteristic-class polynomials. The integral Pontryagin evaluation identity uses rational multiplicativity and Z→Q injectivity; it does not assert an integral tangent/normal class identity.
Assume AC. For every k≥0 the products of CP^{2j} indexed by partitions of k form a Q-basis of Ω_{4k}^SO⊗Q. Equivalently Ω_*^SO⊗Q is the polynomial algebra on [CP²],[CP⁴],[CP⁶],….

For the smooth Stiefel section space over S^m, evaluation at x₀ is a Hurewicz fibration. A nonempty fixed-value fibre is homotopy equivalent, after reference-section disk transport, to based maps S^m→V_m(R^n). A simply connected Stiefel fibre gives a noncanonical component bijection with π_m; vanishing π_m gives connected sections when n≥m+1 and sections exist.

Assume AC_ω. For n≥m+2, regular homotopy classes of S^m→R^n are noncanonically classified by π_m(V_m(R^n)); for n=m+1 they are noncanonically classified by π_m(SO(m+1)), with injectivity supplied by the target-rotation loop argument.

Assume AC_ω. Oriented plane-circle immersions are regularly homotopic if and only if their rotation numbers agree. Rotation number gives a bijection of regular homotopy classes with Z; nonzero-fold circles realize nonzero integers and the Gerono lemniscate realizes zero.

Assume AC. For n≥0 and x=c₁(γ*), CP^n has integral ring Z[x]/(x^{n+1}) and positive top pairing one. Its Euler sequence splits noncanonically to C⊕TCP^n≅(γ*)^{⊕(n+1)}, giving c(TCP^n)=(1+x)^{n+1} and p(TCP^n)=(1+x²)^{n+1}.

concerns.concern: The Hatcher AT source locator says “§5.1, cohomology spectral sequences and multiplicative structure, printed pp.543–549”. The opened [Hatcher PDF](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf), contents on PDF pages 2–4 and preface on page 6, has no Chapter 5 and explicitly excludes spectral sequences; these printed pages are bibliography/index material. The local proof supplies the calculation through declared prerequisites, so this is a source-location correction rather than an identified logical failure.

Its second Hatcher AT reference includes “§5.1 Theorem 5.3, printed pp.526–532”. The opened [Hatcher PDF](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf), complete contents on PDF pages 2–4, ends its chapters with Chapter 4; printed pp.526–532 belong to the appendix, not a spectral-sequence Theorem 5.3. The locally supplied transfer and Serre induction do not depend on this nonexistent locator.

The source locator identifies the cell-attachment argument on printed pp.351–353 as “§4.L”. The [Hatcher contents](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf), PDF page 4, place cellular/CW approximation in §4.1 and §4.L at printed p.487. The proof correctly uses the local high-relative-cells supplier; the bibliography section label needs correction.

Proof 3.1 says “Items 2 and 4 give the rational and odd-prime field isomorphisms through D” without identifying those items. Its Facts do not establish a numbered item list resolving that reference. Steps 1.1–2.1 prove the general comparison and the finite-detector consumer explicitly supplies the needed vanishing, but this illustrative reference should name its suppliers.
